Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

Scope: andesim scripts/ directory, setup.sh, config.env.example, Dockerfile.runtime, and the root ./andesim wrapper. Find legacy: unused scripts (nothing calls them — grep both repos, docs, and other scripts), dead functions inside scripts, stale env vars/options for removed features (QEMU2, in-tree verilator/QEMU builds), commented-out blocks kept "just in case". List what each scripts/* file is and who calls it.

16	# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
17	# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
18	# under nounset).
19	_hybrid_setup_main() {
20	  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
21	    emulate -L sh
22	    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
23	  else
24	    local -
25	    set -euo pipefail
26	  fi
27	
28	  # QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR are NOT in this local list: they are exported
29	  # for the caller's shell at the end of this function, and exporting a local
30	  # dies at function return (the shell pops the scope, children never see it).
31	  local ROOT PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE _arch
32	  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
33	  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
34	  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
35	  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
36	  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
37	  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
38	  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
39	  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
40	
41	  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
42	  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }

44	
45	  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
46	  clean_plugin() {
47	    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
48	    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
49	      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
50	    else
51	      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
52	    fi
53	    ok "plugin cleaned"
54	  }
55	
56	  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
57	    case "${2:-all}" in
58	      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
59	      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
60	      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
61	      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
62	    esac
63	    return 0
64	  fi
65	
66	  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
67	  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
68	    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
69	      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
70	      return 1
71	    fi
72	    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
73	    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"

126	  esac

135	  export VSIM_BIN_DIR

137	  export VSIM_QEMU32="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv32"

141	  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"

3	# Self-bootstraps on first use so a fresh clone can run ./andesim
4	# directly; the build is host-only (no Verilator/SystemC/QEMU needed).
5	#
6	# macOS is run-only: both legs must share one Linux kernel, so the wrapper
7	# re-execs inside the prebuilt runtime image (podman machine VM); the shared
8	# mmap then lives in the VM, never on a virtiofs mount. ANDESIM_OS is a
9	# test hook to force the branch from Linux.
10	set -euo pipefail
11	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
12	
13	if [ "${ANDESIM_OS:-$(uname -s)}" = "Darwin" ]; then
14	  exec bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_in_container.sh" "$@"
15	fi
16	
17	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
18	[ -x "$BIN" ] || bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >&2
19	exec "$BIN" "$@"
20

1	# andesim runtime image -- for run-only hosts (macOS via podman machine).
2	#
3	# Built ON LINUX (CI or a Linux workstation); macOS users only pull it:
4	#
5	#   podman build -f Dockerfile.runtime \
6	#     --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=<verilator env image> \
7	#     -t andesim-runtime:latest .
8	#
9	# BASE_IMAGE is the vsim build environment from verilator/Dockerfile
10	# (target `env`) -- the same image scripts/build_vsim.sh uses, so the
11	# Verilator/SystemC toolchain and QEMU build deps are already there.
12	# The publish registry/name is still an open question; consumers override
13	# the local default with ANDESIM_IMAGE.
14	#
15	# The whole repo is baked, fully built, at /opt/hybrid_sim, so the baked
16	# ./andesim resolves every artifact via its normal repo-relative paths
17	# (build/qemu, engines, plugin, runtime). scripts/run_in_container.sh
18	# invokes that path as the entry; the user's cwd is bind-mounted only for
19	# ELF inputs and outputs.
20	ARG BASE_IMAGE=andes-vsim-env:latest
21	FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}
22	
23	COPY . /opt/hybrid_sim
24	WORKDIR /opt/hybrid_sim
25	
26	# Build: plugin -> driver -> runtime. Both QEMU and vsim are NOT built here --
27	# they are integrated as external prebuilt binaries; provide them at run time, e.g.
28	#   -v /path/to/qemu/build:/qemu:ro   -e VSIM_QEMU=/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
29	#   -v /path/to/vsim/build:/vsim:ro   -e VSIM_BIN_DIR=/vsim
30	# (the plugin builds against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h, so
31	# no QEMU source tree is needed; the driver discovers cycle engines by scanning
32	# $VSIM_BIN_DIR). setup.sh is NOT used here -- it locates the external qemu/vsim,
33	# which are mounted at run time, not build time.
34	RUN make -C qemu_plugin \
35	 && ./scripts/build_driver.sh \
36	 && make -C runtime
37	
38	ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/hybrid_sim/andesim"]
39

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# build_all.sh -- build the andesim artifacts. This is the entry point that
3	# replaced the former `andesim build` subcommand (which moved out of the driver
4	# binary). It only orchestrates the existing build scripts / Makefiles; the
5	# build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
6	#
7	# Usage:
8	#   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
9	#
10	# TARGET (default: all):
11	#   all       setup.sh (locate external qemu + vsim + plugin) then
12	#             fixtures (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib too)
13	#   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
14	#   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
15	#   runtime   build/runtime/ (rv64) + build/runtime/rv32/ (rv32, when
16	#             HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set): libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o,
17	#             andesim.ld, andesim.specs, include/andesim/ROI.h
18	#
19	# --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
20	#
21	# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
22	# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
23	set -euo pipefail
24	
25	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
26	
27	TARGET=all
28	DRY_RUN=0
29	for arg in "$@"; do
30	  case "$arg" in
31	    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
32	    all|plugin|fixtures|runtime) TARGET="$arg" ;;
33	    *)
34	      echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
35	      echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|plugin|fixtures|runtime] [--dry-run]" >&2
36	      exit 2
37	      ;;
38	  esac
39	done
40	
41	# run one step: print it under --dry-run, otherwise banner + execute (inheriting
42	# stdio so the user watches the build live). set -e aborts on the first failure.
43	run() {
44	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
45	    printf '%s\n' "$*"
46	    return
47	  fi
48	  printf '[build_all] %s\n' "$*"
49	  "$@"
50	}
51	
52	# plugin: build_qemu_plugin.sh wraps `make -C qemu_plugin`; plugins build against
53	# the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h (no QEMU source tree needed).
54	case "$TARGET" in
55	  all)      run bash "$ROOT/setup.sh"; run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
56	  plugin)   run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh" ;;
57	  fixtures) run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
58	  runtime)  run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_runtime.sh" ;;
59	esac
60

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Build the andesim driver: driver/ -> build/andesim.
3	#
4	# Standalone C++20 target (no Verilator, SystemC, or QEMU). Depends only on
5	# the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header under include/. This is the
6	# bootstrap consumed by setup.sh and `andesim build --what driver` (wired in
7	# F14). Out-of-tree build under build/driver; the binary is redirected to
8	# build/andesim via CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.
9	set -euo pipefail
10	
11	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
12	BUILD="$ROOT/build/driver"
13	
14	cmake -S "$ROOT/driver" -B "$BUILD" \
15	  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
16	  -DCMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY="$ROOT/build" \
17	  >/dev/null
18	
19	cmake --build "$BUILD" -j"$(nproc)"
20	
21	echo "built: $ROOT/build/andesim"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Build the user-facing andesim runtime (runtime/) for both arches. Produces:
3	#   build/runtime/       libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs,
4	#                        include/andesim/ROI.h   (rv64; link -B build/runtime)
5	#   build/runtime/rv32/  the same, rv32          (rv32; link -B build/runtime/rv32)
6	# Users link with `-B <dir> -specs=andesim.specs` (USER_GUIDE.md section 5).
7	#
8	# rv64 always builds (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 builds too when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32
9	# is set. Self-contained: fills either toolchain from config.env (exported env
10	# wins), like setup.sh, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
11	set -euo pipefail
12	
13	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
14	SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
15	CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
16	CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
17	
18	[[ -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]] || { echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2; exit 1; }
19	
20	# Capture exported values (they win), then source config.env to fill any gaps.
21	ENV_TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
22	ENV_TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}"
23	if [[ -z "$ENV_TC64" || -z "$ENV_TC32" ]]; then
24	  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
25	    [[ -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]] \
26	      || { echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
27	    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
28	    echo "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchains live elsewhere" >&2
29	  fi
30	  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
31	  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
32	fi
33	[[ -n "$ENV_TC64" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$ENV_TC64"
34	[[ -n "$ENV_TC32" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$ENV_TC32"
35	
36	# rv64 (required).
37	if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" || ! -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin" ]]; then
38	  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset or has no bin/; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
39	  exit 1
40	fi
41	make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv64 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
42	echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a (rv64)"
43	
44	# rv32 (optional: needs the second toolchain).
45	if [[ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}" && -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}/bin" ]]; then
46	  make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv32 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32"
47	  echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a (rv32)"
48	else
49	  echo "skipped rv32 runtime: set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 in $CONFIG_FILE to build it" >&2
50	fi
51

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
3	# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
4	# workspace.
5	#
6	# Env overrides:
7	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
8	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
9	#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
10	#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
11	#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
12	#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
13	#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
14	#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
15	#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
16	#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
17	#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
18	#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
19	#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
20	#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)
21	
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
25	# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
26	# VSIM_QEMU); fall back to the legacy in-tree build only if it is unset.
27	VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}"
28	HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
29	TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"
30	
31	VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
32	VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
33	if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
34	  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
35	  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
36	  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
37	  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
38	  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
39	  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
40	  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
41	  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
42	    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
43	  fi
44	fi
45	
46	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
47	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
48	warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
49	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
50	
51	require() {
52	  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
53	    fail "$1 not found: $2"
54	    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
55	    exit 1
56	  fi
57	}
58	require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
59	require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
60	require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"
61	
62	export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN
63	
64	REQUIRED_ELFS=(
65	  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
66	  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
67	  rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
68	  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
69	  rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
70	)
71	need_build=0
72	for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
73	  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
74	done
75	if (( need_build )); then
76	  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
77	  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
78	fi
79	
80	# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
81	# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
82	# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
83	# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
84	RT_TESTS=(
85	  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
86	  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
87	  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
88	  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
89	  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
90	  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
91	  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
92	  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
93	  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
94	  "rt_m_ext_counters|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_counters"
95	  "rt_m_ext_trigcause|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_trigcause"
96	  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
97	  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
98	  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
99	  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
100	  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
101	  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
102	  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
103	  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
104	  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
105	  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
106	  "rt_c_dlm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_dlm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=DLM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
107	  "rt_c_ilm_code|FIXTURE=rt_c_ilm_code CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=ILM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1"
108	  "rt_c_hvm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_hvm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=HVM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
109	)
110	
111	NEG_TESTS=(
112	  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
113	  "rt_lm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_lm_transport_off.sh"
114	  "rt_hvm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_hvm_transport_off.sh"
115	)
116	
117	# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
118	# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
119	# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
120	# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
121	# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
122	# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
123	# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
124	# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
125	SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
126	  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
127	  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
128	)
129	
130	MODE="${MODE:-both}"
131	case "$MODE" in
132	  marker|pc|both) ;;
133	  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
134	esac
135	
136	default_jobs() {
137	  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
138	  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
139	  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
140	    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
141	    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
142	      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
143	      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
144	    fi
145	  fi
146	  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
147	  printf '%d\n' "$n"
148	}
149	JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
150	[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
151	  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }
152	
153	FILTER="${FILTER:-}"
154	
155	LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
156	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
157	RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
158	LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
159	: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
160	: > "$LOCK_FILE"
161	
162	# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
163	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
164	# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
165	# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
166	# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
167	# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
168	# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
169	run_one() {
170	  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
171	  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
172	  local start end elapsed status rc
173	  start=$(date +%s)
174	  set +e
175	  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
176	  rc=$?
177	  set -e
178	  end=$(date +%s)
179	  elapsed=$((end - start))
180	  case $rc in
181	    0)  status=PASS ;;
182	    77) status=SKIP ;;
183	    *)  status=FAIL ;;
184	  esac
185	  (
186	    flock 9
187	    case "$status" in
188	      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
189	      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
190	      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
191	    esac
192	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
193	      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
194	  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
195	}
196	
197	# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
198	# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
199	# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
200	declare -a WORKPLAN=()
201	for tm in marker pc; do
202	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
203	  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
204	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
205	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
206	    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
207	    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
208	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
209	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
210	    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
211	  done
212	done
213	for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
214	  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
215	  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
216	  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
217	  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
218	done
219	
220	# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
221	# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
222	declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
223	for tm in marker pc; do
224	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
225	  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
226	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
227	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
228	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
229	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
230	    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
231	  done
232	done
233	
234	TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
235	step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"
236	
237	# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
238	# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
239	# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
240	# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
241	# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
242	# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
243	SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
244	mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
245	exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
246	rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
247	for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
248	  printf '.\n' >&8
249	done
250	
251	i=0
252	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
253	  i=$((i+1))
254	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
255	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
256	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
257	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
258	  read -r -u 8 _tok
259	  (
260	    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
261	    printf '.\n' >&8
262	  ) &
263	done
264	wait
265	exec 8>&-
266	
267	# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
268	for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
269	  i=$((i+1))
270	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
271	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
272	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
273	  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
274	  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
275	done
276	
277	declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
278	declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
279	declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
280	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
281	while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
282	  case "$r_status" in
283	    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
284	    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
285	    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
286	          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
287	  esac
288	done < "$RESULTS_FILE"
289	
290	# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
291	# deterministic post-run failure dump.
292	for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
293	  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
294	  w_rest="${w#*|}"
295	  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
296	  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
297	                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
298	  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
299	    echo
300	    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
301	    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
302	  fi
303	done
304	
305	echo
306	marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
307	pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
308	neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
309	total_pass=$((marker_p + pc_p + neg_p))
310	total_fail=$((marker_f + pc_f + neg_f))
311	total_skip=$((marker_s + pc_s + neg_s))
312	step "summary: marker ${marker_p}p/${marker_f}f/${marker_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
313	if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
314	  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
315	  exit 1
316	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
3	# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
4	#
5	# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
6	#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
7	#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
8	#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]
12	#
13	# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
14	# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
15	# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
16	set -uo pipefail
17	
18	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
19	
20	DRY_RUN=0
21	PHASES=()
22	for arg in "$@"; do
23	  case "$arg" in
24	    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
25	    unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
26	    *)
27	      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
28	      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
29	      exit 2
30	      ;;
31	  esac
32	done
33	[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)
34	
35	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
36	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
37	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
38	
39	pass=0
40	failed=0
41	declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
42	
43	# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
44	run_case() {
45	  local name="$1"; shift
46	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
47	  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
48	  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
49	  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
50	    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
51	  else
52	    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
53	    cat "$log"
54	  fi
55	  rm -f "$log"
56	}
57	
58	run_unit() {
59	  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
60	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
61	    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
62	    return
63	  fi
64	  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
65	    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
66	  fi
67	  shopt -s nullglob
68	  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
69	  shopt -u nullglob
70	  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
71	    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
72	  fi
73	  local t
74	  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
75	}
76	
77	run_contract() {
78	  step "[contract] driver feature + parity contracts"
79	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
80	    printf '  %s\n' "tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (each)" \
81	      "tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh (each)"
82	    return
83	  fi
84	  local s
85	  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh \
86	           "$ROOT"/tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh; do
87	    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
88	    run_case "[contract] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
89	  done
90	}
91	
92	run_e2e() {
93	  step "[e2e] hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips"
94	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "scripts/run_e2e.sh"; return; fi
95	  run_case "[e2e] run_e2e.sh" bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
96	}
97	
98	for p in "${PHASES[@]}"; do
99	  case "$p" in
100	    unit)     run_unit ;;
101	    contract) run_contract ;;
102	    e2e)      run_e2e ;;
103	  esac
104	done
105	
106	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
107	  echo
108	  echo "(dry-run: nothing executed)"
109	  exit 0
110	fi
111	
112	echo
113	step "summary: $pass passed, $failed failed"
114	if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
115	  fail "failed: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
116	  exit 1
117	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Hot inner-loop detector wrapper (system-mode, baremetal RISC-V).
3	#
4	# Runs a baremetal ELF under qemu-system-<arch> with the hotloops plugin
5	# and prints a sorted table of detected backward branches:
6	#
7	#   iters | start_pc -> end_pc | function:offset
8	#
9	# Usage:
10	#   scripts/hotloops.sh [opts] <elf>
11	#
12	# Options:
13	#   --arch <riscv32|riscv64|auto>   Target arch (default: auto)
14	#   --qemu <path>                   Override qemu-system binary
15	#   --plugin <path>                 Override plugin .so
16	#   --machine <name>                -M <name> (default andes_ae350)
17	#   --cpu <spec>                    -cpu <spec>
18	#                                   (default andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024)
19	#   --qemu-config <file>            -readconfig <file> (e.g. AE350 device cfg)
20	#   --cwd <dir>                     chdir before launching QEMU so semihosting
21	#                                   opens (fread of bin/*.bin) resolve
22	#   --qemu-arg <arg>                Append an extra arg to the QEMU command
23	#                                   (repeatable)
24	#   --limit <N>                     Top-N loops to print (default 50)
25	#   --min-iters <N>                 Drop loops with fewer than N iters (default 1)
26	#   --objdump <path>                Override objdump (resolves symbols)
27	#   --addr2line <path>              Override addr2line (resolves source lines)
28	#   --no-source                     Disable source file:line resolution
29	#   --raw                           Print raw plugin output, no formatting
30	#   --optimize-rvv                  Only report loops with at least one RVV
31	#                                   instruction (default: on)
32	#   --no-optimize-rvv               Disable the RVV-only filter
33	#   --llm                           Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM
34	#                                   consumption: TL;DR + per-loop fact-sheets
35	#                                   with stable IDs, source snippets, RVV
36	#                                   instruction listings, nesting, and direct
37	#                                   callees (default: on).
38	#   --no-llm                        Emit the plain human-readable table.
39	#   -h | --help                     Show help
40	
41	set -euo pipefail
42	
43	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
44	ROOT="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"  # andesim repo root (this script's parent)
45	
46	ARCH="auto"
47	QEMU=""
48	PLUGIN=""
49	LIMIT=50
50	MIN_ITERS=1
51	OBJDUMP=""
52	ADDR2LINE=""
53	NO_SOURCE=0
54	RAW=0
55	OPTIMIZE_RVV=1
56	LLM=1
57	MACHINE="andes_ae350"
58	CPU="andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024"
59	QEMU_CONFIG=""
60	QEMU_CWD=""
61	EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS=()
62	
63	usage() { sed -n '2,39p' "$0"; exit 0; }
64	
65	# --- arg parsing ---
66	ELF=""
67	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
68	    case "$1" in
69	        --arch)        ARCH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
70	        --qemu)        QEMU="$2"; shift 2 ;;
71	        --plugin)      PLUGIN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
72	        --machine)     MACHINE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
73	        --cpu)         CPU="$2"; shift 2 ;;
74	        --qemu-config) QEMU_CONFIG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
75	        --cwd)         QEMU_CWD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
76	        --qemu-arg)    EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS+=("$2"); shift 2 ;;
77	        --limit)       LIMIT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
78	        --min-iters)   MIN_ITERS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
79	        --objdump)     OBJDUMP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
80	        --addr2line)   ADDR2LINE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
81	        --no-source)   NO_SOURCE=1; shift ;;
82	        --raw)         RAW=1; shift ;;
83	        --optimize-rvv)    OPTIMIZE_RVV=1; shift ;;
84	        --no-optimize-rvv) OPTIMIZE_RVV=0; shift ;;
85	        --llm)             LLM=1; shift ;;
86	        --no-llm)          LLM=0; shift ;;
87	        -h|--help)     usage ;;
88	        -*) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
89	        *)
90	            if [[ -z "$ELF" ]]; then
91	                ELF="$1"; shift
92	            else
93	                echo "error: unexpected positional arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
94	            fi ;;
95	    esac
96	done
97	
98	[[ -n "$ELF" ]] || { echo "error: ELF path required" >&2; exit 2; }
99	[[ -f "$ELF" ]] || { echo "error: not found: $ELF" >&2; exit 2; }
100	
101	# --- arch detection ---
102	if [[ "$ARCH" == "auto" ]]; then
103	    file_out="$(file -L -- "$ELF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
104	    case "$file_out" in
105	        *"ELF 64-bit"*"RISC-V"*)  ARCH=riscv64 ;;
106	        *"ELF 32-bit"*"RISC-V"*)  ARCH=riscv32 ;;
107	        *) echo "error: cannot auto-detect arch (not RISC-V?), pass --arch" >&2; exit 2 ;;
108	    esac
109	fi
110	
111	# --- locate qemu + plugin ---
112	# QEMU is an externally-built binary: QEMU_BIN_DIR (config.env, exported by
113	# setup.sh) holds qemu-system-{riscv32,riscv64}. The plugin builds out-of-tree
114	# under qemu_plugin/ (make -C qemu_plugin), never into QEMU.
115	if [[ -z "$QEMU" ]]; then
116	    QEMU="${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/build/qemu}/qemu-system-${ARCH}"
117	fi
118	[[ -x "$QEMU" ]] || { echo "error: qemu not found/executable: $QEMU" >&2; exit 2; }
119	
120	if [[ -z "$PLUGIN" ]]; then
121	    PLUGIN="${ROOT}/qemu_plugin/libhotloops.so"
122	fi
123	[[ -f "$PLUGIN" ]] || { echo "error: plugin not built: $PLUGIN (run: make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT=\$PWD/QEMU)" >&2; exit 2; }
124	
125	# --- run ---
126	# Temp files are declared up front so one EXIT trap covers every exit path,
127	# including the early --raw exit before SYMS/LINES/DISASM are created.
128	LOG="$(mktemp -t hotloops.XXXXXX.log)"
129	SYMS="" LINES="" DISASM=""
130	trap 'rm -f "$LOG" "$SYMS" "$LINES" "$DISASM"' EXIT
131	
132	QEMU_CMD=("$QEMU"
133	          -plugin "${PLUGIN},limit=${LIMIT},min_iters=${MIN_ITERS}"
134	          -d plugin -D "$LOG"
135	          -M "$MACHINE"
136	          -cpu "$CPU"
137	          -nographic -semihosting
138	          -bios "$ELF")
139	[[ -n "$QEMU_CONFIG" ]] && QEMU_CMD+=(-readconfig "$QEMU_CONFIG")
140	[[ ${#EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS[@]} -gt 0 ]] && QEMU_CMD+=("${EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS[@]}")
141	if [[ -n "$QEMU_CWD" ]]; then
142	    ( cd "$QEMU_CWD" && "${QEMU_CMD[@]}" ) >/dev/null
143	else
144	    "${QEMU_CMD[@]}" >/dev/null
145	fi
146	
147	if [[ "$RAW" -eq 1 ]]; then
148	    cat "$LOG"
149	    exit 0
150	fi
151	
152	# --- symbol table from objdump (best effort) ---
153	if [[ -z "$OBJDUMP" ]]; then
154	    for cand in llvm-objdump riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump \
155	                riscv32-unknown-elf-objdump objdump; do
156	        if command -v "$cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
157	            OBJDUMP="$cand"
158	            break
159	        fi
160	    done
161	fi
162	
163	SYMS="$(mktemp -t hotloops_syms.XXXXXX)"
164	LINES="$(mktemp -t hotloops_lines.XXXXXX)"
165	DISASM="$(mktemp -t hotloops_disasm.XXXXXX)"
166	if [[ -n "$OBJDUMP" ]]; then
167	    # Capture FUNC symbols: addr size type name
168	    "$OBJDUMP" -t "$ELF" 2>/dev/null \
169	        | awk 'tolower($0) ~ /[ \t]f[ \t]/ && NF>=5 {
170	                  addr=strtonum("0x" $1);
171	                  size=strtonum("0x" $(NF-1));
172	                  name=$NF;
173	                  if (size>0) print addr, size, name;
174	              }' \
175	        | sort -n -k1,1 > "$SYMS" || true
176	
177	    # Capture disassembly: each output line is "<hex-pc> <mnemonic> <operands>".
178	    # Works for both GNU binutils objdump and llvm-objdump. Used by the RVV
179	    # filter (mnemonic) and --llm mode (operands, callee names).
180	    if [[ "$OPTIMIZE_RVV" -eq 1 || "$LLM" -eq 1 ]]; then
181	        "$OBJDUMP" -d --no-show-raw-insn "$ELF" 2>/dev/null \
182	            | awk '
183	                /^[ \t]*[0-9a-fA-F]+:[ \t]+[^ \t]+/ {
184	                    line = $0;
185	                    sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line);
186	                    sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", line);
187	                    sub(/:[ \t]+/, " ", line);
188	                    print line;
189	                }' > "$DISASM" || true
190	    fi
191	fi
192	
193	# --- locate addr2line for source line resolution (DWARF) ---
194	if [[ "$NO_SOURCE" -eq 0 && -z "$ADDR2LINE" ]]; then
195	    for cand in llvm-addr2line addr2line \
196	                riscv64-unknown-elf-addr2line riscv32-unknown-elf-addr2line \
197	                riscv64-linux-gnu-addr2line; do
198	        if command -v "$cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
199	            ADDR2LINE="$cand"
200	            break
201	        fi
202	    done
203	fi
204	
205	# Pre-collect all PCs from the log and batch-resolve to file:line.
206	# LINES file format: <hex-pc> <file:line>
207	if [[ "$NO_SOURCE" -eq 0 && -n "$ADDR2LINE" ]]; then
208	    pcs="$(awk -F',' '/^0x/ {gsub(/[ \t]/,"",$1); gsub(/[ \t]/,"",$2); print $1; print $2}' "$LOG" | sort -u)"
209	    if [[ -n "$pcs" ]]; then
210	        # addr2line: -e <elf> reads addrs on stdin, prints file:line.
211	        # We keep full paths here (no -s) so --llm mode can locate the
212	        # source file for code snippets; table mode basenames in Python.
213	        out="$(printf '%s\n' $pcs | "$ADDR2LINE" -e "$ELF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
214	        paste <(printf '%s\n' $pcs) <(printf '%s\n' "$out") > "$LINES" || true
215	    fi
216	fi
217	
218	# --- format ---
219	python3 - "$LOG" "$SYMS" "$LINES" "$DISASM" "$LIMIT" "$MIN_ITERS" \
220	        "$OPTIMIZE_RVV" "$LLM" "$ELF" <<'PY'
221	import sys, os, re, bisect
222	
223	log_path     = sys.argv[1]
224	syms_path    = sys.argv[2]
225	lines_path   = sys.argv[3]
226	disasm_path  = sys.argv[4]
227	limit        = int(sys.argv[5])
228	min_iters    = int(sys.argv[6])
229	optimize_rvv = int(sys.argv[7]) == 1
230	llm_mode     = int(sys.argv[8]) == 1
231	elf_path     = sys.argv[9]
232	
233	# --- symbols (FUNC syms): list of (addr, size, name) sorted by addr ---
234	syms = []
235	try:
236	    with open(syms_path) as f:
237	        for line in f:
238	            parts = line.split()
239	            if len(parts) >= 3:
240	                syms.append((int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]),
241	                             " ".join(parts[2:])))
242	except FileNotFoundError:
243	    pass
244	
245	def resolve(pc):
246	    for addr, size, name in syms:
247	        if addr <= pc < addr + size:
248	            return f"{name}+0x{pc-addr:x}"
249	    return "?"
250	
251	# --- source map: pc -> "path:line" (full path; basename in Python for table) ---
252	src_map = {}
253	try:
254	    with open(lines_path) as f:
255	        for line in f:
256	            parts = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t", 1)
257	            if len(parts) == 2:
258	                pc_str, src = parts
259	                src = src.strip()
260	                if src and not src.startswith("??"):
261	                    try:
262	                        src_map[int(pc_str, 16)] = src
263	                    except ValueError:
264	                        pass
265	except FileNotFoundError:
266	    pass
267	
268	def src_full(pc):
269	    return src_map.get(pc, "")
270	
271	def src_basename(s):
272	    """Basename the path part of a 'path:line[ (extra)]' string."""
273	    if not s:
274	        return ""
275	    head, sep, tail = s.partition(" ")
276	    return os.path.basename(head) + (sep + tail if sep else "")
277	
278	def src_short(pc):
279	    return src_basename(src_full(pc))
280	
281	# --- disassembly: pc -> (mnemonic, operands) ---
282	disasm = {}
283	try:
284	    with open(disasm_path) as f:
285	        for line in f:
286	            line = line.rstrip("\n")
287	            parts = line.split(None, 2)
288	            if len(parts) < 2:
289	                continue
290	            try:
291	                pc = int(parts[0], 16)
292	            except ValueError:
293	                continue
294	            mnemonic = parts[1]
295	            operands = parts[2] if len(parts) >= 3 else ""
296	            disasm[pc] = (mnemonic, operands)
297	except FileNotFoundError:
298	    pass
299	
300	disasm_pcs = sorted(disasm.keys())
301	
302	def is_rvv_mnemonic(mn):
303	    mn = mn.lower()
304	    return mn.startswith("v") and len(mn) > 1 and mn[1].isalpha()
305	
306	rvv_pcs = sorted(pc for pc, (mn, _) in disasm.items() if is_rvv_mnemonic(mn))
307	
308	def rvv_insns_in_range(s, e):
309	    out = []
310	    if not rvv_pcs or s > e:
311	        return out
312	    i = bisect.bisect_left(rvv_pcs, s)
313	    while i < len(rvv_pcs) and rvv_pcs[i] <= e:
314	        pc = rvv_pcs[i]
315	        mn, ops = disasm[pc]
316	        out.append((pc, mn, ops))
317	        i += 1
318	    return out
319	
320	CALL_MN = {"jal", "jalr", "c.jal", "c.jalr"}
321	CALLEE_RE = re.compile(r"<([^>]+)>")
322	
323	def calls_in_range(s, e):
324	    out = []
325	    if not disasm_pcs or s > e:
326	        return out
327	    i = bisect.bisect_left(disasm_pcs, s)
328	    while i < len(disasm_pcs) and disasm_pcs[i] <= e:
329	        pc = disasm_pcs[i]
330	        mn, ops = disasm[pc]
331	        if mn in CALL_MN:
332	            m = CALLEE_RE.search(ops)
333	            target = m.group(1) if m else "(indirect)"
334	            out.append((pc, mn, target))
335	        i += 1
336	    return out
337	
338	def parse_file_line(s):
339	    """'path:42' or 'path:42 (discriminator 1)' -> (path, 42)."""
340	    if not s or s.startswith("??"):
341	        return None, None
342	    m = re.match(r"^(.+?):(\d+)(?::\d+)?(?:\s|$)", s)

# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
#   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
#                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
#                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
#                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.

TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
fi

hybrid_resolve_paths() {
  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$TOP_ROOT/verilator/build}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$TOP_ROOT/build/qemu}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
      exit 77
    fi
  done
}

# Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
# $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
# absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
hybrid_describe_int() {
  "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
}

# Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
# the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
put_word_le() {
  local v=$3 bytes="" i
  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
  done
  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
}

# hotloops - hot inner-loop detector

Detects the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
translation-block transitions in `qemu-system-<arch>`. For each detected
loop you get the loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, and the iteration
count. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.

Two parts ship together:

- `contrib/plugins/hotloops.c` - QEMU TCG plugin that records edges.
- `scripts/hotloops.sh` - wrapper that runs the plugin and formats output.

## Usage

```
scripts/hotloops.sh [options] <elf>
```

The wrapper launches `qemu-system-<arch>` with `-bios <elf>` on a baremetal
machine (default `andes_ae350`) and a vector-capable CPU (default
`andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024`). Override per the options below
for other targets.

### Options

| Flag                | Default            | Description                                                    |
|---------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--arch <a>`        | auto               | Target arch: `riscv32`, `riscv64`, or `auto` (from `file`).    |
| `--qemu <path>`     | auto               | Override the `qemu-system-<arch>` binary.                      |
| `--plugin <path>`   | auto               | Override the plugin `.so`.                                     |
| `--machine <name>`  | `andes_ae350`      | `-M <name>` passed to QEMU.                                    |
| `--cpu <spec>`      | `andes-ax45mpv,...`| `-cpu <spec>` passed to QEMU. Default enables RVV 1.0 vlen=1024.|
| `--qemu-config <f>` | -                  | `-readconfig <file>` (e.g. AE350 device cfg).                  |
| `--cwd <dir>`       | -                  | `chdir` before launching QEMU (so semihosting `fread` of `bin/*.bin` resolves). |
| `--qemu-arg <arg>`  | -                  | Extra arg appended to the QEMU command. Repeatable.            |
| `--limit <N>`       | 50                 | Print at most N loops.                                         |
| `--min-iters <N>`   | 1                  | Drop loops with fewer than N iterations (hot-loop threshold).  |
| `--objdump <path>`  | auto               | Override objdump (for `function+offset` and disassembly).      |
| `--addr2line <path>`| auto               | Override addr2line (for source-line resolution).               |
| `--no-source`       | off                | Skip source resolution even if DWARF is present.               |
| `--raw`             | off                | Print raw plugin output (CSV-ish), no formatting.              |
| `--optimize-rvv`    | on                 | Only report loops that contain at least one RVV instruction.   |
| `--no-optimize-rvv` | off                | Disable the RVV-only filter; report all loops.                 |
| `--llm`             | on                 | Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption (see below).  |
| `--no-llm`          | off                | Emit the plain human-readable table instead of the LLM report. |

### Build prerequisites

The plugin lives in `contrib/plugins/`. Build once:

```
ninja -C build contrib-plugins
```

It is incremental on subsequent edits to `hotloops.c`. The QEMU binaries
themselves (`qemu-system-riscv64`, `qemu-system-riscv32`) do **not** need
to be rebuilt.
